headline: The AI earnings night turned into a de-gross: INTC's crowded long breaks, AMZN is sold but defended, memory falls on good prints, and META/MSFT become the megacap hide.
market_read: Desks moved from yesterday's single-name split to a broad tech de-gross. Jefferies (Favuzza, 29 Oct) says it has been net for sale in tech for five weeks, BofA (Villani, 29 Oct) sees long-only funds' biggest monthly selling of 2026, and UBS PB (Ruple, 30 Oct) says de-grossing hit both sides of the book while short exposure stays above the 80th percentile, which leaves room for a squeeze. INTC (-23-25%) was the crowded long that broke: every desk is negative and BofA Research downgraded it. AMZN (-7%) missed the AWS bogey, but most desks (JPM Schilsky, UBS Dwyer, Bernstein Seidman, 30 Oct) defend it on the >40% 2027/28 AWS guide, while Jefferies and TMTB stress it is still crowded. Memory (SNDK, Kioxia, Hynix) and the MRVL-LITE optics debate add to semis pressure, with META, MSFT and ORCL's funding relief named as the places to hide.

up.why: AMZN fell ~7% on a 3Q AWS miss (+39% vs a ~43% buyside bogey), but most desks defended it. JPM (Schilsky, 30 Oct) says the 'vast majority' of investors defended it. UBS (Dwyer, 30 Oct) calls the feedback 'more forgiving' and frames it as an EPS-revision story. Bernstein (Seidman, 30 Oct) calls it a 'treat' into re:Invent. The narrative is the first multi-year AWS guide (>40% in 2027 and 2028) and the $578bn backlog. Positioning remains the risk: Jefferies (Wong, 29 Oct) and TMTB (30 Oct) both say it is still a crowded long, and TMTB notes the guide is below buyside FY27 AWS bars, so buyside curves come down even as the Street's go up. JPM's desk (Heavey, 30 Oct) adds a lingering equity-raise fear. AMZN is not in the Bloomberg X rising/falling lists (through 29 Oct) and has no HOT/BULL analog row in monitor.json, so the desk evidence carries this read alone. Over 1-5 days it trades with the Nasdaq de-gross. Over 2-4 weeks the case is Street estimate revisions plus re:Invent after the midterms.
up.confirm: Street FY27/28 AWS estimates move to ~40%+ and desks report long-only buying into weakness rather than HF trimming; no equity-raise headline.
up.weaken: An equity or large debt raise, or buyside FY27 EPS bars keep drifting lower (TMTB: ~$12) while the crowded long unwinds.

up.why: Two desks name META as the place money goes inside megacaps after the GOOGL and AMZN prints. JPM's TMT desk (Heavey, 30 Oct) calls it 'the clear beneficiary' as it works back toward the $625 offering price. Jefferies (Wong, 29 Oct) hears investors gravitating to MSFT and META as the cleaner megacaps. Jefferies (Favuzza, 29 Oct) ranks the tactical pecking order MSFT, META, AMZN, GOOGL. In monitor.json (through 29 Oct) META's HOT score is 64.5 (60-<80 band) against a BULL of 39.9, so attention is ahead of tone. Its own-history 5-session HOT analog is thin (n=7, median -0.9%), so it is not a forecast. Over 1-5 days, META is a relative-strength hide inside a weak Nasdaq. Over 2-4 weeks, the test is whether it reclaims the offering price.
up.confirm: META trades back above the $625 offering price on a down Nasdaq day, and more desks report rotation out of GOOGL/AMZN into META.
up.weaken: Megacap de-grossing turns indiscriminate (UBS PB: de-grossing from both sides of the book) and META loses the offering price again.

up.why: AMD reports on 3 Nov and the INTC miss puts it in focus. JPM's semis specialist (Meyers, 30 Oct) reads INTC's CFO non-answer on AMD's server guide as AMD out-execution, sees no incremental read-through, and has AMD at +3 on his buyside survey. Jefferies (Favuzza, 29 Oct) hears a ~$17bn guide midpoint. Positioning there is split: there is less HF length than in late September, but AMD is still the long-only favourite. The divergent view is UBS (Ruple, 30 Oct) and BofA Research (Arya, relayed 30 Oct), who both flag a PC/supply-gap read-across to AMD. AMD is not in the Bloomberg X movers and has no HOT/BULL analog row. Over 1-5 days it trades with semis (SOXX -6% pre-market per JPM). Over 2-4 weeks the print and the server-CPU share narrative decide.
up.confirm: Server CPU guide confirms share gains while INTC is supply-constrained, and HF length rebuilds after the print.
up.weaken: The PC weakness INTC flagged shows up in AMD client guidance, or the +3 survey bar proves too high.

up.why: This carries over from 29 Oct. BofA sales (Villani, 29/30 Oct) says the investor-day funding plan (a final $20bn vs ~$50bn feared) tightened ORCL CDS ~60bp and the BofA hyperscaler credit basket 13bp, and that 'funding sentiment may have inflected'. JPM's desk (Heavey, 30 Oct) adds that ORCL 'pretty much has to tell investors they are done raising capital'. In monitor.json (through 29 Oct) ORCL is HOT 44.3 / BULL 48.0, both mid-band; its own-history 5-session analogs are a median +0.6% (57% up, n=28) for HOT and +1.2% (56% up, n=39) for BULL, which is no edge. Over 1-5 days the credit tightening helps it hold up in an AI de-gross. Over 2-4 weeks it needs the credit move to stick.
up.confirm: ORCL CDS keeps tightening (credit_workbook) and desks report long-only adds, not only short covering.
up.weaken: A new financing headline or OCI customer-concentration scare reopens the funding debate.

up.why: JPM's TMT desk (Heavey, 29 Oct session) saw semicaps outperform on KLAC's print, with money rotating into the group. BofA Research (Arya, relayed 30 Oct) says INTC's capex plans read positive for semicaps, and JPM (Meyers) notes INTC's equipment purchase orders rose ~40% q/q. Bloomberg X (through 29 Oct) has KLAC among the rising names, z 1.55 (Δz +1.68). monitor.json has HOT 57.6 / BULL 44.5; the own-history 5-session BULL analog median is +1.0% (62% up, n=39), and the HOT analog median is -0.3% (46% up). This is one desk plus a read-across, and the 30 Oct semis sell-off (-6% pre-market) works against it near term, so conviction is low. Over 2-4 weeks, the INTC capex step-up ('up strongly' in 2027) is the supportive narrative.
up.confirm: Semicaps keep outperforming SOX on down days and more desks cite rotation into WFE.
up.weaken: Semicaps trade down with memory and SOX, with no relative strength, or capex-peak talk returns.

down.why: INTC was a crowded long going into the print: JPM's buyside survey had it at +4 on 29 Oct, and Bernstein (Seidman, 30 Oct) calls it 'a crowded long into the print'. It then guided 4Q revenue ~$15.5bn vs ~$17.1bn Street, and the stock is about -23% to -25%. Every desk read is negative. Barclays (Rand, 29 Oct) expects holders to go to the sidelines. Jefferies (Favuzza, 29 Oct) heard 'no defending'. JPM (Meyers, 30 Oct) says the lack of a cover bid means it 'may take time'. UBS (Ruple, 30 Oct) expects old execution concerns to return. BofA Research (Arya) downgraded it to Neutral, PO $100. Management (MS Risom, 29 Oct) calls 2027 an investment year with negative FCF. INTC is not in the Bloomberg X movers (through 29 Oct) and has no analog row. Over 1-5 days, expect the crowded length to keep unwinding. Over 2-4 weeks, Bernstein sees it 'in the penalty box until the 4Q print'.
down.confirm: Further estimate cuts or downgrades, and desks report long-only exits rather than HF covering.
down.weaken: A supply-unlock or foundry-customer headline brings dip buyers in. Bernstein notes the pre-market move may already price most of it.

down.why: This carries over from 29 Oct. Jefferies (Favuzza, 29 Oct) says a lot of HF length came out on NOW's worst-ever day, but only ~7.6% of the float turned over, which is low for a drawdown of that size. That means the unwind may not be finished, or that holders did not capitulate. Barclays (Rand, 30 Oct) points to how crowded NOW had become and to renewed SaaS concern. JPM's desk (30 Oct) says NOW is still 'on the dead lows' while some enterprise SaaS is being covered. GS (Callahan, 29 Oct) calls it a 'show-me story' into CY27 guidance. In monitor.json (through 29 Oct) NOW is HOT 49.2 / BULL 51.3; its own-history analogs (median +1.0%/+0.8% at 5 sessions) are pre-gap and no guide to the path after a -25% day.
down.confirm: NOW stays pinned on the lows while peers bounce, and float turnover catches up with continued HF/LO selling.
down.weaken: Bulls step in on the ~19x CY28 non-GAAP EPS framing (GS) and SaaS covering broadens to NOW.

down.why: SNDK beat and guided above the Street, yet it fell ~4-8%. Jefferies (Wong, 29 Oct) and JPM (Meyers, 29/30 Oct) both say there was a long lean and positioning was still reasonably high. Barclays (Rand, 29 Oct) says shrinking beats make it hard to convince bears that the cycle is not late. The memory tape around it is weak: Kioxia missed its 3Q guide badly (MS Amerian, 30 Oct) and Hynix fell -7% on foreign selling (Jefferies Beavington, 30 Oct). The divergent view is Bernstein (Seidman, 30 Oct), which calls SNDK a 'treat' with mostly positive feedback, and Jefferies hears bottom-fishing in memory in small size near ~1x forward P/B. SNDK is not in the Bloomberg X movers (through 29 Oct) and has no analog row. Over 1-5 days, crowding unwinds with SOX. Over 2-4 weeks, the NBM/LTA durability debate decides.
down.confirm: Memory keeps underperforming on good news (MU, Kioxia) and desks report long-only trimming.
down.weaken: Bottom-fishing turns into real buying after the midterms, or the split and buyback attract a new holder base.

down.why: RDDT fell ~18-20% after hours after missing on revenue and US DAUs, and it warned that Google search referrals are down 'meaningfully'. Jefferies (Favuzza, 29 Oct) confirms a short lean going in, so the shorts were right. JPM (Schilsky, 30 Oct) calls the quarter 'a mess'. This is weakening sentiment more than a crowding unwind, because the stock was not crowded long. RDDT is not in the Bloomberg X movers (through 29 Oct) and has no analog row. Over 1-5 days, shorts may press into the DAU-decline warning. Over 2-4 weeks, any Google-traffic stabilisation or licensing news is the swing factor.
down.confirm: Weekly referral data keeps falling and estimate cuts follow.
down.weaken: Short covering on a licensing deal, or logged-in DAU strength reframes the story.

down.why: Most of the >25 investors JPM (Meyers, 30 Oct) polled on the reported MRVL-LITE talks 'largely view [COHR] as a loser', citing TRx competition, doubts on 6-inch wafer execution and OCS. COHR scores -1 on JPM's survey into its 4 Nov print. This reverses the 29 Oct JPM idea that COHR would come into the spotlight as the last independent laser player. A few clients still see M&A optionality. In monitor.json (through 29 Oct) COHR is HOT 43.3 / BULL 46.4; the own-history 5-session BULL analog median is +2.7% (66% up, n=41), but that predates this feedback. This is one desk's survey, so conviction is low. Over 1-5 days, read it into the 4 Nov print.
down.confirm: Optics names weaken into prints (LITE at 0 and COHR at -1 on JPM survey) and COHR lags LITE on deal headlines.
down.weaken: A COHR M&A or strategic-buyer headline, or a margin beat on 4 Nov.

themes.title: AMZN's multi-year AWS guide: Street catch-up vs buyside step-down
themes.text: AMZN's first-ever two-year AWS guide (>40% in 2027 and 2028) cuts both ways. JPM (Schilsky), UBS (Dwyer) and Bernstein (Seidman), all 30 Oct, treat it as an EPS-revision catalyst the Street must catch up to. TMTB (30 Oct) notes buyside FY27 AWS bars sat at mid-40s to low-50s, so the guide lowers buyside curves (buyside FY27 EPS settling near ~$12 per TMTB, vs ~$13.50 Bernstein hears). Jefferies and TMTB still call it a crowded long. These figures are attributed as given, not reconciled.

themes.title: De-gross and rotation: flows say sell tech, retail buys the dip
themes.text: This is desk flow data with no company ticker, so it is not logged as observations. Jefferies (Favuzza, 29 Oct) has net sold >$10bn of tech over 20 days and has been net for sale five straight weeks. BofA (Villani, 29 Oct) says long-only funds are on track for their biggest monthly net selling of 2026 and that semis were sold all October at 2x September's pace, while retail is on six straight weeks of buying. UBS PB (Ruple, 30 Oct) says de-grossing came from both sides of the book, with short exposure >80th percentile over 5 years, which leaves room for a short-covering rally. Susquehanna derivatives (30 Oct) still sees upside call buying in SMH/SOXX/DRAM. Barclays (Rand, 30 Oct) says most semis investors will not re-gross until after earnings and the midterms.

themes.title: MRVL-LITE: deal priced at ~30% premium, optics peak-or-not debate
themes.text: JPM (Meyers, 30 Oct) polled >25 investors. They assign high odds to the talks being real, but question why a LITE that is sold out through 2029 would sell. Bears read it as a laser-cycle top, and bulls as an all-in CPO/NPO bet by MRVL. JPM's arb specialist puts the implied premium at ~30%, with a 65-70% closing probability. The view that COHR loses reverses JPM's own prior-day spotlight idea, so the divergence is kept visible.

themes.title: Memory: good prints, bad reactions
themes.text: SNDK beat and fell. Kioxia's 3Q guide missed buyside by ~¥0.4tn (MS Amerian, 30 Oct). Hynix fell -7% on W1.5tn of foreign selling (Jefferies, 30 Oct). Barclays (Rand) cites WDC's next-day underperformance despite a 20% EPS revision as the most concerning semis reaction. Jefferies (Wong) hears small-size bottom-fishing at ~1x forward P/B, and BofA sales still pitches MU/Hynix (Franco, 29 Oct). No DAMNANG or SemiAnalysis note in the window offered an independent read.

coverage_gaps: No DAMNANG or SemiAnalysis e-mail arrived in the window, so there is no independent-author check on the memory or optics reads.

Bloomberg X attention and the HOT/BULL analogs in monitor.json run through 29 Oct, before the AMZN/INTC/SNDK/RDDT after-hours moves. AMZN, INTC, SNDK, RDDT and AMD have no analog rows, so for them the read rests on desk evidence. The step-3 rebuild refreshes the data.
Messages before ~13:08Z on 29 Oct were covered by the 29 Oct review and were not re-logged. That includes the earlier GOOGL/MSFT/NOW feedback from the same desks.

Screened but not read in full: Jefferies' Taiwan/ASE note, JPM Global Specialist (30 Oct), GS 'What Matters Today', Citrini threads, Irrational Analysis/Beyond The Hype on INTC, Vik's Newsletter and FundaAI on MRVL-LITE. Research PDFs (UBS, BofA, JPM, MS) were treated as research, not desk color.
Macro flow statistics (Jefferies net selling, BofA long-only selling, UBS PB short exposure) carry no company ticker. They appear in market_read and themes only.
source_notes: Channel outlook-com via desk_mail_collect.ps1; inbox lag 0 h; 1,117 messages screened, 386 bodies pulled, 34 read in full or in part (registered desk senders first). Newest received 2026-10-30T13:02:06Z.

Desk and specialist-sales voices carry no ratings or PTs. The INTC downgrade (Arya, Neutral, PO $100) and the NVDA valuation point are BofA Research relayed in Franco's sales one-liners, logged as 'Research relay'.
TMT Breakout is a paid independent newsletter, not a broker, and is logged as an independent author.

Desks differ on the size of the moves (INTC -15% to -25% depending on timestamp, SNDK +2.7% to -8%). Each figure is attributed as given. Buyside AMZN FY27 EPS bars also differ: ~$12 (TMTB) vs ~$13.50 (Bernstein).
Weighting is editorial: multi-desk agreement (INTC, AMZN, NOW) weighs more than single-desk ideas (KLAC, COHR, FLEX). Survey scores (JPM) are logged as investor feedback, not positioning data.
